new.title: Display switcher and toolbar icons in Tech View and Board View match the design
preconditions: You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View, Work orders > Create & Edit and See financial data, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
The design pictures DC-01-toolbar-tech-view-light-1440.png and DC-01-toolbar-board-view-light-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.
In the design pictures the names, numbers, dates and amounts are sample data, and the rank numbers (1, 2, 3 …) beside rows and cards are left out of this release, so do not compare those.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC01 Ana Icons) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC01 Toolbar Icons") is used by this case only.
Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17801) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
steps: Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
Click List in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar.
Look at the three buttons of the display switcher.
Click Tech View in the display switcher.
Look at the display switcher, the density button and the column chooser button, and compare them with the Tech View design picture.
Click the density button.
Look at the menu that opens.
Press Escape.
Click Board View in the display switcher.
Look at the display switcher and the density button, and compare them with the Board View design picture.
Click List in the display switcher.
Look at the other icons in List's toolbar.
results: Step 3: the switcher shows three outline icons side by side in a light-grey rounded track: a bulleted list (List), the head and shoulders of a person (Tech View) and a square board with three bars of different lengths (Board View), the same three drawings as in the design pictures and about the same size as in the pictures at 100% zoom (20 px in the PRD). They are thin-line outline icons of the same weight, not filled icons, emoji or text characters.

Step 5: the Tech View button sits on a white raised segment and the other two look flat. The density button shows three lines with an up-and-down arrow at their right (the design's "row-height" icon) and the column chooser button shows a rectangle split into three columns (the design's "columns-3" icon), drawn in the same thin outline style, as in the Tech View picture.
Step 7: the density menu offers Compact, Regular and Comfortable, with Regular marked as the one in use.

Step 10: the Board View button is now the white raised segment, and the density button shows a different drawing from Tech View's: a card with an up-and-down arrow (the design's "card-height" icon), as in the Board View picture.
Step 12: the other icons in List's toolbar look the same as in List in production today; only the display switcher is new.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10049 (Story 6, Density); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 52 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S1-R9a, S1-R9, S6-R1 and Goals, read 14 Oct 2026; Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html", states states__work-orders__tech-density-menu__light__1440 and core__work-orders__board-detailed__light__1440 (design pictures DC-01-toolbar-tech-view-light-1440.png, DC-01-toolbar-board-view-light-1440.png, rendered from that export at the width in the name), read 14 Oct 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

doc_part1: Sign in as an Owner or Admin user. On a QA site click the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". This is {User-A}. To check the permissions: your initials (top right) > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders: View and Create & Edit are on (the Admin role has full access, See financial data included).

Pick one location for the whole case; it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (to change it: your initials > Change Location). This is {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Create everything below at {Location-A}.

Use a screen at least 1440 px wide (1536 px or wider if the case names 1536 px). Set the browser zoom to 100% (Ctrl+0, or Cmd+0 on a Mac). To give the window an exact width without developer tools, use a window-size browser extension (for example Window Resizer for Chrome) and choose 1440 × 900; it shows the size it set.

Open this case in TestRail and download the design pictures named in the Preconditions from the case's attachments. Open each in an image viewer at 100% (actual size) and place it beside the browser window.

Your initials > Settings > Staff. Reuse a staff member only if they are active, have Time Clock on, {Location-A} in Location and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User. Otherwise click New Staff Member and enter First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC01 Ana Icons), an Email with ZZAUTOTEST in it, Role Technician, at least one Department (required), Location {Location-A}, turn Time Clock on, then Save & Close. This is {Technician-A}.

Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC01 Toolbar Icons") > Save. This is {Customer-A}; use it for this case only. On the customer page click Contacts > New Contact > First Name and Last Name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Contact) > Save. Then Assets > New Asset > pick the contact, Year (for example 2022), Make (type "Freight" and pick Freightliner), Model (for example M2), Unit (for example TRK-118) > Save. Contact and Make are required.

Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick {Customer-A} and its asset > Save (if a Confirmation about the credit limit appears, click Create). The work order opens on its Lines tab with the New Line form. In What Are You Doing? type "grease" and pick the ready-made line "Service - Full grease service", turn Line Approved on and click Save & Close. The status reads Approved. Write down the number shown at the top left (for example S10043-17801). This is {Work-order-1}. On {Work-order-1}'s page pick {Technician-A} in the Lead Technician dropdown; it saves at once (the dropdown shows once the work order is Approved).

Work Orders > All: open each filter in the filter bar and clear any selection, turn Assigned to me off, empty Search, and set density to Regular with the density button (the icon button with lines and an up-and-down arrow, to the left of the display switcher).
Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All > Tech View shows a group for {Technician-A} holding {Work-order-1}, and the display switcher shows List, Tech View and Board View.

Your browser window is 1440 px wide, with the browser zoom at 100%.
For the steps that name 1536 px, your screen lets you widen the window to 1536 px.
The design pictures DC-04-tech-view-header-row-1440.png and DC-04-tech-view-all-columns-1440.png are open beside the app at 100% zoom (actual size); they are attached to this case.

In the design pictures the header row starts with a collapse arrow and a position-number column, and two labels read "Unit #" and "Assigned Tech": the first two are left out of this release and the labels follow the PRD (Unit, Assigned Techs), so do not compare those.
Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST DC04 Dan Columns) is an active technician at {Location-A}.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST DC04 Default Columns") is used by this case only.
Approved work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17810) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A}.
On the Work Orders page nothing is chosen in any filter, Assigned to me is off, Search is empty and density is Regular (the default).
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Tech View in the display switcher.
Read the column header labels from left to right, scrolling the table sideways to see them all.
Compare the size, weight and colour of the header labels with the row text under them and with the design picture.
Look at the space between each pair of neighbouring header labels.
Click the column chooser button.
Turn on On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician, and every other column the chooser offers that is off.
Press Escape.
Scroll the table sideways from left to right and look at every header label.
Click the density button and choose Compact, and look at the header labels.
Click the density button and choose Comfortable, and look at the header labels.
Widen the window to 1536 px and look at the header labels again.
results: Step 2: there are 13 columns, in this order: Status, Waiting On Parts, Number, Customer, Unit, Asset, Progress, Service Advisor, Clocked In, Lines, Assigned Techs, Created on, Total price. On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are not shown.

Step 3: the header labels are small (12 px in the design, visibly smaller than the 14 px row text under them), medium weight (not bold) and grey (lighter than the dark row text), as in the design picture.
Step 4: no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour; there is clear space between every pair.
Step 6: On Site, VIN/Serial # and Lead Technician are offered and can be turned on.
Step 8: with every column on, no header label touches, overlaps or is cut off by its neighbour, as in the all-columns design picture.
Steps 9 and 10: the header labels keep the same size, weight and grey colour at Compact and at Comfortable.
Step 11: at 1536 px no header label touches or overlaps its neighbour.
